issues.legal_issue: A landlord may apply for action concerning a rental building that is about to fall vacant before the building is actually vacant.
material_facts: The landlord applied for release of the building while an eviction suit against the tenant was pending and before the tenant had been physically dispossessed.
The eviction decree was later passed and possession was delivered to the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The application was maintainable before the building actually fell vacant because the building was about to fall vacant.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(1)(a) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 authorizes action concerning a building that is vacant, has fallen vacant, or is about to fall vacant. Actual vacancy is therefore not a prerequisite to applying. The Court relied on the text of the provision and cited no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.rental_vacancy_allocation_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding in which a landlord seeks action concerning the vacancy or allocation of a rental building.
predicates.building_about_to_fall_vacant: The landlord applied while eviction of the tenant was being pursued and before possession had been delivered, so the building was expected to become vacant.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks action concerning a rental building in a vacancy proceeding and eviction is expected to make it vacant, the application may be made before actual vacancy.

issues.legal_issue: An objector need not be heard in a vacancy-release proceeding when the objector has established no right to the premises and a hearing would not affect the outcome.
material_facts: The objector claimed to be a partner in the hotel business and sought to prevent the landlord from taking possession, but never possessed the premises.
The objector did not establish that he was a subtenant or had a right to the premises, and his suit seeking to set aside the eviction decree was dismissed.
The landlord received possession under the eviction decree, and the vacancy was then notified.
issues.conclusion: The objector was not entitled to a hearing before the vacancy was notified or the building was released, because his asserted interest had not been established and a hearing would have been futile.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, in the circumstances, no hearing was required where the objector had no established claim or right to the property and hearing him would have led to the same result. The Court relied on the circumstances of the proceedings and cited no earlier cases on this issue.

rule.if: vacancy_release_proceeding and objector_never_possessed_premises and objector_failed_to_establish_right and challenge_to_eviction_decree_failed

predicates.vacancy_release_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding to notify a rental building's vacancy or release it to the landlord.
predicates.objector_never_possessed_premises: The objector never occupied or possessed the premises.
predicates.objector_failed_to_establish_right: The objector failed to establish that he was a subtenant or otherwise had a right to the premises.
predicates.challenge_to_eviction_decree_failed: The objector's related suit seeking to set aside the eviction decree was dismissed.

issues.definition: In a vacancy-release proceeding, an objector who never possessed the premises, established no right to them, and failed to overturn the eviction decree need not be heard.
